To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NAC, cysteine or its S-propyl or S-ethyl analogues can significantly decrease the hepatic TAG and cholesterol content, and protect the liver against oxidative damage in mice consuming a high fat diet.

the intake of NAC (1 g/l), SPC (1 g/l) and SEC (1 g/l, 1·5 g/l) significantly decreased hepatic TAG and cholesterol contents via lowering the activity of lipogenic-related enzymes, and protecting liver from oxidative damage in mice consuming a high saturated fat diet.

the intake of NAC and cysteine-containing analogues, SEC and S-Propyl cysteine, significantly decreased the activity and mRNA level of lipogenic-related enzymes, malic enzyme, FAS and HMGCoA reductase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of NAC, SPC and SPC, which may be used as a dietary supplement for preventing and treating obesity and related diseases, such as hyperlipidaemia and hepatic steatosis.
the effects of cysteine-related compounds on hepatic TAG and cholesterol biosynthesis, and oxidative stress in mice consuming a high saturated fat diet.
the effects of cysteine-related compounds on hepatic TAG and cholesterol biosynthesis and anti-oxidant protection in mice consuming a high saturated fat diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NAC, SPC and SEC are potent agents for preventing high saturated fat-associated hepatic lipogenesis and lipid peroxidation.
NAC, SPC and SEC are potent agents for reducing the high saturated fat-associated risk of obesity and fatty liver.

the intake of NAC and cysteine-containing amino acids can protect against high saturated fat-induced lipid metabolism disorders and oxidative stress in liver, and the intake of cysteine is beneficial for improving the antioxidant capacity in liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intake of NAC (or SEC or SPC) could significantly decrease hepatic TAG and cholesterol contents via inhibiting the lipogenic-related enzyme activities and mRNA expression, and alleviating the high-saturated fat-induced oxidative stress.
the cysteine-containing agents, NAC, SEC & SPC, are potent agents for preventing high-saturated fat-induced oxidative stress and liver lipid accumulation in mice.
cysteine-containing agents, especially NAC, SPC or SEC, could serve as potential functional agents in preventing or treating obesity-related diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NAC, SPC and SEC have the potential to be developed as a functional food or nutraceutical for the prevention or treatment of hyperlipidaemia and liver damage.
NAC, SPC and SEC are effective agents for reducing hepatic TAG and cholesterol levels, and alleviating high-fat diet-associated oxidative damage.
cysteine is a potent agent for preventing high-saturated fat-induced hepatic TAG and cholesterol accumulation.
